thread.title: Mid-Day Update: Intel Powers Dow to Another Record High

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day Update: Intel Powers Dow to Another Record High
text:
Shutterstock photo Powered by gains in component stock Intel ( INTC ), the Dow Jones Industrial Average lunged higher at mid-morning to set another all-time high and extend its winning streak to a fourth day. Although the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are also off their sessions lows and trading in positive territory, gains have been mitigated by pressure on health care and banking stocks.
Stock futures were losing altitude before the opening bell as concerns about the fallout from Italy's 2019 budget weighed on European equities and left investors searching for safe havens, causing further deterioration of Monday's USMCA-fueled rally.
The Dow circled the flatline at the open before racing higher thanks to a sharp rebound in Intel, gaining as much as 5% to set a two-month high. The semiconductor stock was under pressure Monday when analysts cautioned that its battle with Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) could become very costly.
The Dow's move higher is also being amplified by strength in the industrial sector with shares of component stock Boeing ( BA ) at its third straight record high. Apple ( AAPL ), Caterpillar ( CAT ) and Walgreen (WBA) are also contributing to a triple-digit gain in the blue chip index.
The upbeat price action in the US failed to underpin European bourses with all the major indices trading lower. The showdown between the new government in Rome with the European Union prompted Goldman Sachs to warn that "contagion risks have risen" as Italy's bloated budget deficit could raise risks for an exit from the EU. Tuesday's losses were largely to blame on comments from Lega party member and Euro-skeptic Claudio Borghi calling for Italy to adopt its own currency.
Crude oil was down $0.02 to $75.28 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.08 to $75.28 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $16.50 to $1,208.10 an ounce, while silver was up $0.29 to $14.80 an ounce. Copper was up $0.02 to $2.81 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was down 0.38% to $15.89 with the United States Natural Gas Fund up 1.94% to $26.21. Among precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 2.24% to 18.95 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 1.27% to $114.00. The iShares Silver Trust was up 2.02% to $13.89.
